DesignGroutMix.gml:name: MIX-A — Very Severe (Mg<1000) Design Mix

Remark.content: Per 70-TMSS-03 Rev.02 Table 8B, appended in full to GBL-24136-Geotech-Final-Report.pdf (and its own extracted copy, GBL-24136-Geotech-Report-MA .xlsx) - documents not available when this design was first authored. CORRECTED from an earlier version that used the Table 8B row for Mg>1000 ppm (Type I cement, Fly Ash admixture, max W/BM=0.36): GBL-24136 5.4.3's own chemical analysis (BS 1377 Part 3) measured magnesium at 571-954 ppm across all three tested boreholes/depths - every value below 1000 ppm - while sulphate (5810-8515 ppm) and chloride (0.510-0.705%) both clear the >2000 ppm / >0.10% thresholds, and the site is stated as Very Severe exposure. That combination selects a DIFFERENT row of the same table: Type I (C3A 8-14%) cement with Silica Fume admixture, max W/BM=0.40, min binding material 390 kg/m3 (cement+SCM), max Cl in concrete 0.10%, min f'c 38 MPa (Note 1) - not the Fly Ash/0.36 row this design used before.

Table 8B fixes only the cement type, admixture type, the maximum W/BM ratio and the minimum binder content - it states no batch recipe, and neither FMSA24047-FTR-CMC-00 nor GBL-24136-Geotech-Final-Report (nor their extracted CMC-Final-Report-Extracted.xlsx / GBL-24136-Geotech-Report-MA .xlsx workbooks) states one either. The proportions below are therefore an INFERRED, illustrative design meeting the stated constraints, not a project-specified recipe: an 8% silica fume replacement of total binder by mass (within ACI 234R's typical 5-10% dosage range for durability applications - a literature value, not project-stated); the maximum W/BM (0.40) used directly as the design value, matching how the earlier Fly Ash version used its own ceiling (0.36); an assumed 2% air content; and specific gravities cement=3.15 (Table 8B), silica fume=2.2 (typical/literature, not project-stated), sand=2.65, water=1.0. Mix proportions expressed per 1 m3 of concrete.

Three compressive strength figures appear in the project record, for different purposes. 25 MPa is the structural design value (FMSA24047-FTR-CMC-00 Table 4 and its extracted copy, CMC-Final-Report-Extracted.xlsx) - also the fck used in modulusDesign below. 30 MPa is the owner's minimum for construction, set in National Grid SA's review of submittal DTS-091 R03 (ref. 30501201/35327-J/24, 13/11/2024, comment 7: construction 30 MPa, design 25 MPa; the contractor accepted it); it is the acceptance threshold in crit-grout-strength-qc-min and crit-grout-strength-qc-mean, applied to all 41 batches because nothing in the record shows the grout design changed after the letter. 70-TMSS-03 Table 8B Note 1 separately sets f'c >= 38 MPa for Very Severe/Severe exposure - a durability, not a structural, minimum. strengthDesign here keeps the higher, governing 38 MPa value; all three are satisfied in practice, with margin.

modulusDesign is newly populated (previously absent - the element exists for exactly this purpose, per its own schema documentation, but had never been instantiated on this object). EY = 3700 x fck^(1/3), per ASIRI 2012 Clause 3.1.1.4 as cited in FMSA24047-FTR-CMC-00 Section 6, fck = 25 MPa (the report's own "not less than" design value) -> EY = 10,818,866 kPa (~10.82 GPa). This is the CMC column stiffness the settlement calculation (FMSA24047-FTR-CMC-00 Sections 6/8) uses, distinct from strengthDesign.

One mix design covers the whole program, confirmed on this pass, not one per zone: FMSA24047-FTR-CMC-00 Section 8 states a single method and a single set of governing standards applied uniformly across all nine zones (matching the single-basis finding already recorded on RIProgramBasis[ripb-01]); the Load Transfer Platform is a separate, non-cementitious compacted granular fill (DesignRILTP), not a second grout/concrete mix. No additional DesignGroutMix is warranted. CMC-Final-Report-Extracted.xlsx also carries real per-batch field data (41 batches, 1,099 CMCs, cast 14-Oct-2024 to 16-Dec-2024, 7-day and 28-day cylinder strengths, all 41 batches passing the 25 MPa threshold, 28-day range 40.7-54.5 MPa/average 46.6 MPa) that the still-open "realized grout batch instances" phase (NEXT_SESSION.md) can draw on directly - not built here, out of this task's scope, but recorded so that phase does not have to rediscover the source.

activityType corrected from "aggregate" to "test" (2026-09-28, Dan's own instruction, GB5) - diggs:PlannedActivityTypeEnumType's own documentation defines "aggregate" as "will create a sample or samples by aggregating EXISTING SAMPLES" (sampleScope should then cite more than one sourceSampleRef), which does not describe this design: a grout mix is produced by blending raw constituents (cement, SCM, aggregate, water), not by combining existing samples. "test" - "will produce a test, standard or blank sample that does not relate to any field sample or sampling feature" - is the value that actually matches, the identical correction just applied to the realized side (diggs:SamplingActivity[sa-gb-1]'s own activityType).

The numbers are the contractor's installation sequence numbers from the production coordination summary. A grid column is placed by its node of DRC-G1 or DRC-G2; an off-grid column by the target position of its single-position design. The 9 unfulfilled Grid 1 nodes are not sequenced.

Owner minimum compressive strength for construction, 30 MPa: National Grid SA review of submittal DTS-091 R03, ref. 30501201/35327-J/24, 13/11/2024, comment 7 (construction 30 MPa, design 25 MPa; the contractor responded that for construction 30 MPa will be considered), in the scanned appendix of FMSA24047-FTR-CMC-00 (PDF pp.61-67). The final report and CMC-Final-Report-Extracted.xlsx sheet "7. Concrete Compressive" (A10/D10) still label the pass/fail threshold with the 25 MPa design value; the owner's higher construction value governs acceptance and is applied to all 41 field batches (all 41 satisfy it; 28-day range 40.7-54.5 MPa). 70-TMSS-03 Rev.02 Table 8B, Note 1 (appended to GBL-24136-Geotech-Final-Report.pdf; clean structured extraction in GBL-24136-Geotech-Report-MA .xlsx sheet "7. Chemical Analysis" row 30) - the durability-governing minimum for Very Severe/Severe exposure, independent of which admixture row applies. Matches DGM-MIX-A's own strengthDesign, which keeps this as the higher, governing value over crit-grout-strength-qc-min's 25 MPa.

Same authority and limit as crit-grout-strength-qc-min (30 MPa, the owner construction minimum; CMC-Final-Report-Extracted.xlsx sheet "7. Concrete Compressive" A70/B70 still shows the 25 MPa design value), stated at the mean statistic rather than the per-batch minimum - mirroring the mean/minimum pair GroutSpecificationType's own strengthAverage/strengthMinimum fields carried before GB4 retired them in favour of sibling PerformanceCriterion objects. The 41 real batches actually achieved 46.58 MPa average (28-day, sheet7 B67) against this requirement, comfortably clearing it - the achieved value is evidence, not restated here as the limit; it belongs on the realized GroutBatch/measurement objects the still-open "realized grout batch instances" phase (NEXT_SESSION.md) will build.

70-TMSS-03 Rev.02 Table 8B (appended to GBL-24136-Geotech-Final-Report.pdf; clean structured extraction in GBL-24136-Geotech-Report-MA .xlsx sheet "7. Chemical Analysis" row 21/F column, "Max Cl in Concrete %") - a fixed 0.10% ceiling across every exposure row regardless of admixture route. The table extract states neither which chloride fraction nor what basis; the limit is read as the WATER-SOLUBLE chloride content, as a mass fraction of the cement (reading of the 70-TMSS-03 text supplied 2026-09-30). Acid-soluble chloride (designProperty.xml#acid_soluble_chloride_content_in_concrete) is a distinct quantity; the extract states no acid-soluble limit, so none is modelled. Modelled as a DesignConformanceCriterion, not a PerformanceCriterion (GB5/GB6): a mix-composition requirement, not an emergent behaviour of the cured material. Compliance is shown by testing (constituent materials and hardened concrete, for example ASTM C1218/C1218M), and no such test is presented for this project, so the criterion is not evaluated - see ev-grout-mix-a. The property is the water-soluble chloride content in concrete - distinct from properties.xml#chloride_content (soil/groundwater, the exposure condition that selects the Table 8B row) - direction-neutral; the "maximum" is carried by operator/limit below.

70-TMSS-03 Rev.02 Table 8B, Very Severe (Mg<1000)/Silica Fume row - "Min. BM Content (Kg/m3)" = 390, the same row DGM-MIX-A's own design uses directly as its binder content. A mix-proportioning requirement verified from the batch record, not a tested physical property - see designProperty.xml#binding_material_content. The property is binding material content, direction-neutral; the "minimum" is carried by operator/limit below, not the property's own name (corrected, GB7, 2026-09-28, Dan's observation - the entry was originally minted as minimum_binding_material_content, inconsistent with every other entry in this dictionary and in properties.xml, none of which bakes a comparison direction into its name).

70-TMSS-03 Rev.02 Table 8B, Very Severe (Mg<1000)/Silica Fume row - "Max W/BM" = 0.40, the same row DGM-MIX-A's own design uses directly as its water/binding-material ratio (distinct from waterCementRatio=0.4348, which excludes the SCM replacement from the denominator). A mix-proportioning requirement verified from the batch record, not a tested physical property - see designProperty.xml#water_binding_material_ratio. The property is water/binding-material ratio, direction-neutral; the "maximum" is carried by operator/limit below (corrected, GB7, 2026-09-28, Dan's observation).

FMSA24047-FTR-CMC-00 work method statement, p.54: "Slump test shall not be lower than 180mm and not greater than 260mm", performed before placement. The method statement does not make clear whether that is once per batch or for every CMC; the criterion is stated per placement and the subject kind of a check (batch or column) would follow whichever applies. Not evaluated: the report presents no slump records. DGM-MIX-A's former slumpDesign of 120 mm was removed - it had no source in the project reports (carried over from an earlier draft) and lies outside this range; the design states no slump target of its own, the acceptance range lives here.

FMSA24047-FTR-CMC-00 work method statement, p.54: compressive strength testing at a minimum of 1 sampling per 100 m3 of concrete placed. Stated as a rate (0.01 per m3). Not evaluated: Appendix 5 reports one averaged strength per age per casting date and does not say how many samplings stand behind it, so the count cannot be shown. Were the samplings recorded, each would be its own sample with its specimens and tests citing it, and one check per batch (that batch the only subject, its 28-day tests the evidence) would compare the count of distinct samplings to the batch volume.

Freyssinet Menard work method statement FMSA-EN24313-MS-CMC Rev 00 (05/09/2024), reproduced in FMSA24047-FTR-CMC-00 Appendix 2, s.9.3, p.9 of 27 (FTR PDF pp.44, 54): "Discharge of concrete, shall be completed within 3 hours after the introduction of mixing water to cement & aggregate" (the same section gives a concrete expiry time of 180 minutes). One specification for the whole program: nothing in the project record varies by zone except the design length, which is stated on the column designs. Technique: Controlled Modulus Columns formed with a 600 mm closed (lost-cap) displacement auger that pushes soil sideways and removes no spoil (FMSA24047-FTR-CMC-00 s.7.1.1-7.1.2), hence columnType drilled_displacement_column and riInstallationMethod full_displacement. Column material is governed by GS-MIX-A. The limits are the sibling criteria that cite this specification through partOfSpecificationRef: crit-col-position, crit-col-length-min, crit-col-length-deviation, crit-col-refusal, crit-col-embedment, crit-col-verticality, and the composites crit-col-depth-or-refusal and crit-col-acceptance.

Method content that states no limit and so is not a criterion: setting out is by the execution drawings from the main axis set out by the general contractor; for each column the operator checks that the machine mast is vertical and well positioned to the setting out (Freyssinet Menard work method statement FMSA-EN24313-MS-CMC Rev 00 (05/09/2024), reproduced in FMSA24047-FTR-CMC-00 Appendix 2, s.9.1, p.9 of 27); depth is controlled by driving to the depth on the approved layouts, the operator recognising the bearing layer by rising hydraulic pressure and falling penetration speed (s.9.2).

Freyssinet Menard work method statement FMSA-EN24313-MS-CMC Rev 00 (05/09/2024), reproduced in FMSA24047-FTR-CMC-00 Appendix 2, s.9.1, p.9 of 27 (FTR PDF pp.44, 54): "the tolerance is 200 mm in each direction". ASSUMPTION (Dan, 2026-10-03): read as a radial distance in plan, 0.20 m; the per-axis reading is available through the easting_position_deviation and northing_position_deviation dictionary entries.

Not evaluated. The deviation needs the designed setting-out coordinates, and the setting-out drawing the inspection requests cite (EN24313-DWG-SD-6001) is not in the project record. Owner minimum length 10 m: National Grid SA review of submittal DTS-091 R03, ref. 30501201/35327-J/24, 13/11/2024 (FMSA24047-FTR-CMC-00 PDF pp.21-28), comment 7 ("minimum length of CMC shall be 10 m"); the contractor adopted it ("the revised report consider the Minimum length of CMC 10.0 m"). An absolute as-built length, distinct from crit-col-length-deviation, which compares length with the design length. A hard requirement: it is a member of crit-col-acceptance.

Length against design: as-built column length minus the design length of the DesignRIColumn the column cites (FMSA24047-FTR-CMC-00 Table 4, p.16, by zone). ASSUMPTION (Dan, 2026-10-03): the sources state no permitted shortfall, so a column should be no shorter than designed (limit 0 m). Driving may stop short of the design depth only at refusal (FTR s.7.1.2 step 2c, "when the required depth is reached or refusal criteria"), so this is one member of crit-col-depth-or-refusal. A failed check here is not by itself a non-conformance; it becomes one only if refusal cannot be shown for that column.

FMSA24047-FTR-CMC-00 s.7.1.2 step 2c (p.12) and the Table 4 note: "refusal criteria (5cm penetration for 2 consecutive minutes)". ASSUMPTION (Dan, 2026-10-03): read as less than 5 cm of total penetration in 2 minutes, not 5 cm per minute; the interval is stated by the interval_duration evidence condition.

Not evaluated. It needs the drilling record of each column (depth against time), and no drilling records exist for this project; the four rig logs at the repo root are from a different job (FMSA 25053, Jubail, 2026).

CompositeAcceptanceCriterion.gml:name: Column driven to design depth OR to refusal

Remark.content: FMSA24047-FTR-CMC-00 s.7.1.2 step 2c: "when the required depth is reached or refusal criteria (...) the driving is stopped". The column is acceptable if it reached its design length or stopped at refusal. Satisfied where the length member is satisfied; otherwise undetermined until refusal is shown from the drilling records.

National Grid SA review of submittal DTS-091 R03, ref. 30501201/35327-J/24, 13/11/2024 (FMSA24047-FTR-CMC-00 PDF pp.21-28), comment 6: the minimum depth of the columns "shall be sufficient enough to cross the Sabkha layers and any lose clayey layers"; the contractor replied that all columns are "fully embedded into the bearing layer, well clear of the sabkha zones". ASSUMPTION (Dan, 2026-10-03): the bearing layer is the shallowest layer of the soil model with a Young's modulus of at least 20000 kPa and no softer layer below it. That is the Silty sand layer (guo-g1-siltysand, top -3.23 m RL) in the Transformers model, the Silty sand to sandy silt layer (guo-g2-siltysandtosandysilt, top -7.86 m RL) in the Buildings model, and the Clean sand to silty sand layer (guo-g3-cleansand, top +2.34 m RL) in the Default Site model. Embedment is the elevation of the layer top minus the column toe elevation; the limit 0 m means the toe is at or below the top of the layer.

Each check cites the bearing layer as its evidenceObservationRef. A column is assigned to a soil model by its plan position against the model footprints (Transformers first, then Buildings, otherwise Default Site), which agrees with its load transfer platform zone for all 1099 columns. The "loose clayey layers" of the comment are not separately modelled.

No numeric limit appears in the project record: Freyssinet Menard work method statement FMSA-EN24313-MS-CMC Rev 00 (05/09/2024), reproduced in FMSA24047-FTR-CMC-00 Appendix 2, s.9.1, p.9 of 27 says only that the operator checks the machine mast is vertical; the owner asked for integrity testing "for confirmation of verticality and soundness" with acceptance criteria (National Grid SA review of submittal DTS-091 R03, ref. 30501201/35327-J/24, 13/11/2024 (FMSA24047-FTR-CMC-00 PDF pp.21-28), comment 8), and the verticality row of CMC_Parameters_Jazera.xlsx is blank. ASSUMPTION (Dan, 2026-10-03): 2 %, horizontal deviation divided by depth, times 100.
Checks are by declaration. The pile integrity tests (ASTM D5882 low-strain) detect cracks and section changes and do not measure inclination, and no inclination was recorded.

Remark.content: The three requirements a column must meet together (Dan, 2026-10-03): the 10 m owner minimum length is a hard requirement; the column must not stop short of the top of the bearing layer; and it must have reached its design depth or refusal. Position and verticality are separate criteria and are not part of this combination.

RIProgramBasis.gml:description: The site-wide basis the Controlled Modulus Column program design was prepared from: the standards it was prepared under, the class of calculation used, the safety format those standards imply, and the ground aggressivity adopted as its durability premise. ONE BASIS FOR THE WHOLE PROGRAM, not one per zone - FMSA24047-FTR-CMC-00 8 states a single method, a single in-house calculation tool and a single set of governing standards applied uniformly across all nine zones, and what varies per zone is the resulting design output, not the premise. Sources are FMSA24047-FTR-CMC-00 (the CMC final technical report) and GBL-GT-24136 (the geotechnical investigation it was prepared from).
RIProgramBasis.gml:name: CMC program design basis

Remark.content: Seven governing standards, which is not simply FMSA24047-FTR-CMC-00 2.2's list. Excluded from that list deliberately: reference [6], "ASTM. American Society for Testing and Materials", names no standard number or year and cannot be resolved to a specification; references [8] MENARD Quality Assurance and Quality Control System & Procedures, [9] OHSAS 18001:2007 and [10] ISO 14001:2004 are contractor management-system and quality-procedure documents governing how the work is executed rather than premises the design was prepared from, so they are out of scope for a program basis (PB4) - they are candidates for the construction-activity side instead. Added beyond that list, because the design demonstrably rests on them although 2.2 omits them: NF P94-261 and NF P94-262 carry the bearing-capacity and skin-friction formulae of 8.2, and SBC 301-CR-18 is the cited source of every seismic parameter in GBL-24136 3.2 Table 1.

safetyFormat is INFERRED and is not stated by the project. FMSA24047-FTR-CMC-00 names no safety format anywhere, and a keyword sweep of both reports returns no "partial factor", "global factor" or any stated factor of safety value (PB4 6.5). The inference rests on 8.2's capacity chain being taken from NF P94-262 (toe bearing q_b, limit skin friction q_s, negative skin friction Ktan-delta) and NF P94-261 (q_net), which are France's Eurocode 7 national application standards and which implement Design Approach 2 - verified 2026-09-23 against CEREMA's own methodological guide to NF P94-262 rather than assumed. Weighed against it: the method actually executed is a pressuremeter/CPT correlation chain using Frank and Zhao (1982) mobilization factors, not a visible partial-factor verification, so DA2 is implied by the standards adopted rather than exercised in the calculation. Recorded as inferred per the convention PB2 established for every inferred value on this program.

Two exposureClassification values, on the two independent axes the property is repeatable for - chemical attack on the concrete and grout, and electrical corrosivity to embedded steel - not one finding stated twice. Both come from GBL-24136 and neither appears in the CMC report at all. sec_tmss_very_severe is from 5.4.3's chemical analysis (BS 1377 part 3: sulphates 5810-8515 ppm, chlorides 0.510-0.705 %, magnesium 571-954 ppm, pH 7.90-8.20), with 7.11 naming 70-TMSS-03 Rev. 02 Table 8B as the authority that sets cement type from it. palmer_very_severe is from 5.2's soil resistivity, where all six ERT stations returned 0.11-0.23 ohm-m against Table 5's 0-10 ohm-m VERY SEVERE band (Palmer 1974).

Fields left absent, checked against the full source set at PB4 rather than assumed: designWorkingLife and consequenceClass (no service life or reliability/consequence class stated anywhere in either report); designMethod and archingModel (both concern LTP load-transfer mechanics, which neither report addresses - the design is a column bearing-capacity calculation); factor (the coefficients 8.2 does state - the rheological factor alpha-M, the penetrometer bearing factor Kc, and the Frank and Zhao mobilization factors Kq and KT - are adopted correlation coefficients, not the partial or global safety factor set a safetyFormat applies, which is what diggs:DesignFactor and this type's factor element are defined for); peakGroundAcceleration (GBL-24136 3.2 Table 1 gives Ss, S1, Fa and Fv but no a_g, and deriving one from them is not code-sanctioned - ASCE 7 and SBC 301 derive site-adjusted PGA from a separately mapped PGA and its own F_PGA coefficient, neither of which the report provides).

References [2] and [3] of FMSA24047-FTR-CMC-00 2.1 ("CMC Design report document reference – FMSA-EN24313-TP" and the General Plot Plan drawing WA 884920 sheet 003 rev. 00) are acknowledged but NOT built as associatedFile: diggs:AssociatedFileType/fileURL is mandatory and neither document is held or retrievable, so no real URL exists to cite and none is fabricated. [1], the geotechnical investigation GBL-GT-24136, is not an associatedFile either but for a different reason - it is already the diggs:Project this program's projectRef targets.

Per-value clauses, all from GBL-24136 3.2 Table 1 and all cited there to SBC 301-CR-18: Ss from Figure 22-1, S1 from Figure 22-2, the site class from Table 20-1 (against SPT N less than 15), Fa from Table 11-1 and Fv from Table 11-2. The report's own prose at 3.2 says "SBC 301-2008" while every row of its table cites SBC 301-CR-18; the 2018 edition is taken as correct because it is what the table rows themselves name.

peakGroundAcceleration is deliberately ABSENT. No a_g is stated anywhere in the project record, and it cannot be derived from the values here: in ASCE 7 and the codes derived from it a site-adjusted peak ground acceleration comes from a separately mapped PGA and its own F_PGA coefficient, whereas Fa and Fv apply only to the spectral ordinates. Synthesising one from Fa and Ss would apply the wrong coefficient to the wrong hazard parameter and present the result as sourced.

seismicSiteClass here is the AS-INVESTIGATED class - the ground as found, read against SPT N less than 15 in the seven boreholes of a pre-construction investigation. It is therefore neither diggs:DesignRITreatedAreaType/seismicSiteClass (the class a design predicts after improvement) nor diggs:RITreatedAreaType/seismicSiteClass (the class achieved). Both of those are left empty on this project, because nothing in the record measures or predicts a post-improvement class.

RigidInclusionSystem.purpose: Project area for Substation 110/13.8 kV S/S — Kingdom of Saudi Arabia

Remark.content: Evaluation of the six acceptance criteria attached to GS-MIX-A (the grout specification of DGM-MIX-A) against the 41 realized GroutBatch objects. FIVE criteria are evaluated: crit-grout-wbm-max and crit-grout-binder-content-min per batch from the value the batch itself records (determination measured); crit-grout-strength-qc-min and crit-grout-strength-durability-min per batch from that batch's 28-day strength test (statisticScope evidence: the source reports one averaged result per batch and age, so the minimum over a batch's evidence is that result; Appendix 5 itself passes or fails each batch); crit-grout-strength-qc-mean once over all 41 batches' 28-day tests (statisticScope population; derived - the mean of the 41 cited results, Appendix 5's 'Average 28-Day Strength').

crit-grout-chloride-max (water-soluble chloride content) is deliberately NOT evaluated. Acceptance against it requires testing - of the constituent materials and of the hardened concrete - and no such test is presented for this project, so there is no value to compare; a design mix does not by its nature put chloride content within a limit, and a declared verdict would assert what nothing supports. The criterion remains in GS-MIX-A. Likewise NOT evaluated: crit-grout-slump (the report presents no slump records) and crit-grout-sampling-frequency (the number of samplings behind each reported strength is not stated).

Synthetic data: every GroutBatch here was synthesized (see each batch's own remark) - the W/BM ratios, and the binding material content (390.0 kg/m3 on all 41, restating the 390 kg/m3 minimum the batches were built from), are not as-batched records. The strength results are the real Appendix 5 28-day averages. Batch 3 is a deliberate nonconformance on W/BM (0.480 against a 0.40 maximum).

Deliberate synthetic nonconformance. The batch also substitutes Fly Ash for the specified Silica Fume SCM; only the W/BM breach is a criterion here. The disposition is a placeholder chosen only because the element is mandatory - no decision about this batch was made.

Evaluation of the criteria attached to RICS-GEN against the 1099 realized RIColumn objects. EVALUATED: crit-col-length-min, crit-col-length-deviation and crit-col-embedment from recorded and modelled values (columnLength, the design length of the cited design, the column centerline and the bearing layer of its soil model), crit-col-verticality by declaration, and the composites crit-col-depth-or-refusal and crit-col-acceptance where they can be determined. NOT EVALUATED: crit-col-position (no designed setting-out coordinates) and crit-col-refusal (no drilling records); crit-grout-discharge-time on GS-MIX-A is not evaluated either (no batching or placement times).

Outcomes: length-min 1099 satisfied (shortest column 10.0 m); embedment 1099 satisfied (smallest embedment into the bearing layer 2.89 m); length-deviation 874 satisfied and 225 not satisfied (222 boundary wall columns built 1 m short of 16 m, 3 outdoor equipment columns 2 m short of 12 m). crit-col-depth-or-refusal and crit-col-acceptance carry a check only where the design length was reached (874 columns, OR satisfied); for the 225 shorter columns the verdict depends on refusal, which cannot be shown without drilling records, so no check is recorded and, deliberately, no NonConformance: a shortfall against design is a member failure, not yet a failure of the requirement.

Synthetic data: the verticality checks are declarations (the 2 percent limit is itself an assumption, see crit-col-verticality), and the embedment values are computed from the column centerline and the layer tops of the three ground models, which are themselves interpretive.
